thread:
sam liu: heads up, production svc-serving in us-west-2 is throwing repeated CUDA illegal memory access errors and a few containers hit OOM during an eviction wave. seeing node gpu-12 flapping. triage needed now.
incident-bot: Incident created: #1769992222 — GPU illegal memory access + OOM cascade on gpu-12 (auto-detected). Paging: high eviction rate detected. Notifying on-call.
maya rao: I'm oncall, joining. sam can you paste the dmesg/kernel log and the container last lines? any customer impact?
sam liu: pasting snippets — cropped for readability:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=3412 0x00000000
[ 1234.567901] kernel: gpu-addr: invalid device addr 0x7ffabcd12345 at vma->vm_end
[ 1234.568000] oom-killer: kill process 4112 (serving-exec) score 987 or sacrifice child
[ 1234.568100] containerd: container 9f3a... exited with status 139
```
sam liu: also see repeated "unaligned memaccess" entries in the module logs, and the serving runtime logs show KV cache lookup faults around the same timestamps.
cheng wu: I'm pulling debug dump from node. attaching corebacktrace + coredump summary. suspect a race between eviction path and preemption handling in our custom cuda kernel shim.
luis garcia: any recent rollout to that fleet?
sam liu: we rolled a runtime patch 2 hours ago that touched eviction ordering and a small preemption fix. traffic was low then but now an eviction surge triggered.
maya rao: ok plan: 1) cordon gpu-12, 2) drain non-critical serving pods, 3) enable fallback routing to dedicated-fallback pool (smaller model variant) for affected tenants, 4) capture full gdb backtrace and preserve dmesg, 5) escalate to runtime/infra. who can cordon and start drain?
cheng wu: starting cordon now: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 --overwrite`
luis garcia: starting drain on non-prod-serving pods: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`
incident-bot: Action logged: node cordoned by cheng wu. Drain initiated.
maya rao: sam can you flip routing? I want the variant fallback active for the tenant buckets hitting errors. Use route-policy: fallback-eviction-2026.
sam liu: flipping policy now — running rollout command:
```
redwoodctl routes set --region us-west-2 --match "tenant:critical" --policy fallback-eviction-2026 --dry-run=false
```
sam liu: done. traffic shows 95% shift to fallback after 20s. error rate for that tenant drops from 18% -> 2% in metrics.
luis garcia: capturing gdb backtrace into S3 (path: s3://redwood-debug/gpu-12/1769992222/). core and perf maps saved.
cheng wu: attaching abbreviated backtrace line: `#0 0x7ffabcd12345 in gpu_kernel_preempt+0x58 (shim.c:412)` then several frames where vm_area->end used after free. this suggests use-after-free in eviction->preempt path.
maya rao: escalation: tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml. @cheng can you collect repro steps and whether running `--disable-async-eviction` reduces hits?
cheng wu: quick test on a repro node with async eviction disabled: ran stress workload, no illegal-access observed after 15m (while normal config showed a repro inside 2m). collecting logs and will open a PR to flip default until patch.
sam liu: customer impact: two tenants saw request failures and higher latency for ~18 minutes during the initial surge. affected request ids: [r-9a3, r-7b2, r-3f5] (we notified support to open outage tickets for any inbound alerts).
maya rao: status update to execs and customers: mitigation in place (fallback routing + cordon). full mitigation ETA depends on runtime patch. can we produce a concise incident summary for postmortem? I'll draft.
luis garcia: note: we observed one container crash with SIGSEGV that leaked GPU pages — added to retention snapshot for postmortem. also increased eviction logging level for 10m to capture more context.
incident-bot: Pager duty: on-call handoff to maya rao at 1769992800.
maya rao: handing off to eng-runtime (cheng/luis) for root-cause and fix rollout. I'm keeping incident open until patch is in prod or rollback is fully applied.
sam liu: root-cause hypothesis: race between async eviction path and preemption handler in our CUDA shim leading to use-after-free of vma/page mapping under load. repro: high eviction + concurrent kernel preemption.
maya rao: next actions (summary):
- eng-runtime to ship hotfix disabling the racy fast-path and restore safe ordering (cheng)
- QA to validate repro and test with stress harness (luis)
- ops to monitor error rates for 2 hours and keep fallback routing live (sam)
- Support to notify affected customers and log incident refs (support assigned)
maya rao: I'm marking priority P1->P2 once error rate stays below 1% for 30m. will update thread.
sam liu: thanks all. preserving all artifacts in s3://redwood-debug/gpu-12/1769992222/ for the PM.
cheng wu: opened runtime PR #2028 with the safety revert; running canary on two nodes now. initial canary shows no regressions and no illegal-access in 25m.
maya rao: keeping channel open for final handoff. good work.
sam liu: closing notes: incident window ~1769992222 -> 1769993999. total impacted requests ~1200 across 2 tenants. fallback routing prevented wider outage. follow-up postmortem assigned to eng-runtime.
